ls: List information about files in the current directory or at path.
-l     Long format: show permissions, owner, and name
ls                List files in current directory
ls -la            Long listing with hidden files
cd: Change the current directory to path. With no arguments, changes
to the home directory. Supports '..' for parent, '~' for home,
TAB completion is available for directory names.
cat: Read the contents of file and print to standard output.
chmod: Change the permissions of files. Only the owner (or root) may do this.
Symbolic:  chmod +x file     add execute for everyone
chmod u+rw file   add read/write for the owner
chmod go-w file   remove write for group and others
The nine characters are three triplets: user, group, other.
rm: Remove files. -r removes directories you created, recursively.
-f ignores missing files. Globs work: rm *.txt
rm save                          reset everything (progress, files, stats)
rm save --filesystem             reset only the filesystem
rm save --filesystem-keep-files  reset, but keep your files (moved to ~)
rm save --dir <path>             restore one directory to its default state
mv: Move source to destination, or rename if in the same directory.
cp: Copy source file to destination. Preserves permissions.
kill: kill - send a signal to a process
Send a signal to a process. Default signal terminates the process.
Use 'ps' or 'top' to find process IDs.
top: Interactive process viewer. Shows CPU usage, memory, and more.
Keys: UP/DOWN select a process, 'k' kills it, 'q' quits.
ps: ps - report a snapshot of current processes
Display currently running processes with PID, command, CPU and
memory usage. Flags like 'aux' and '-ef' are accepted.
grep: grep - search file contents for a pattern
Search for lines matching pattern in file.
-n     Prefix each matching line with its line number
find: find - search for files in a directory hierarchy
Recursively list files and directories. Optionally filter by name
find                List everything under current directory
find /var -name log Find items named 'log' under /var
systemctl: systemctl - control the systemd system and service manager
Drop-in overrides can be placed in /etc/systemd/system/<service>.d/.
head: HEAD(1)
NAME
head - output the first part of files
SYNOPSIS
head [-n N] <file>
DESCRIPTION
Print the first 10 lines of file. Use -n to specify a number.
tail: tail - output the last part of files
Print the last 10 lines of file. Use -n to specify a number.
sudo: sudo - execute a command as root
sudo !!           Re-run last command as root
Execute a command with superuser privileges. You will be prompted
for the password. Authentication is cached for 5 minutes.
python: python - Python scripting in BLTHLL Terminal
Run scripts with 'python <file>' (or 'run'). The file needs execute permission.
Scripts run in a restricted environment with access to standard library functions.
- Open a file using Python's standard open() function
- Example: with open('file.txt', 'w') as f: f.write('text')
- Returns: List of filenames and directories
- Raises FileNotFoundError if file doesn't exist
- Raises FileNotFoundError if file doesn't exist
- Raises FileNotFoundError if file doesn't exist
- Check if path is a file
- Check if path is a directory
# Check if a file is exactly 16 bits
# List all files in current directory
- Scripts have a 5 second execution time limit
- Modules: os, os.path, math, random, string
- Dangerous builtins (exec, eval, compile) are disabled
blsh: A small POSIX-flavoured shell. It supports:
cmd1 | cmd2          pipes (stdout of cmd1 feeds cmd2)
cmd > file           write output to a file (>> appends)
cmd < file           read input from a file
a && b, a || b, a ; b command lists
Ctrl+C       cancel the line (or leave a chat session)
Shift+UP/DN  scroll, PgUp/PgDn page, mouse wheel scrolls

start: With no argument, launches the bullet hell. Waves get harder; every
fifth wave is a boss with timed phases. Survive the phase to beat it.
SHIFT           focus: slow down and show your hitbox
X               bomb: clears bullets (charges as you graze)
Grazing (letting bullets pass very close) builds a multiplier and
charges the bomb. Getting hit resets the multiplier.
Surviving a boss phase without a hit earns a capture bonus.
Beating a boss saves a checkpoint. 'continue' resumes from it.
claude: claude - a parody AI coding assistant
Not the real thing. A handful of keyword rules and templates that
imitate an agentic coding CLI. It never contacts the network and
needs no API key. Ask it whether it's real; it will tell you.
See also: gemini(1), codex(1), copilot(1), ollama(1). They're also fake.
Will not actually write your code. Will give you hints, though.
